title: Applied Unsupervised Learning: reproducible workflows for label-free modelling

creators.name: Ribeiro, Diogo
creators.affiliation: ESMAD - Escola Superior de Media Arte e Design, Instituto Politecnico do Porto

description:
A notebook-first applied unsupervised learning project, built around the argument that unsupervised methods deserve the same discipline as supervised ones: deliberate choice of assumptions, evaluation without labels, and honesty about what a label-free result can support.

Seventeen executed Jupyter notebooks cover customer segmentation, dimensionality reduction and manifold learning, anomaly detection, topic modelling, recommender embeddings, model selection and stability, consensus clustering, streaming clustering with drift monitoring, Dirichlet-process mixtures, dynamic time warping, matrix profiles, unsupervised shapelets, graph community detection and node anomalies, and deep clustering (autoencoder, DEC and contrastive).

They are supported by unsup_lab, a typed and tested Python package providing the reusable machinery: deterministic synthetic data generators, internal clustering metrics, bootstrap and seed stability analysis, and a production layer of CLI, versioned model artifacts, a FastAPI scoring service and a Dockerfile. Every notebook is reproducible from fixed seeds without private data, and the package is held to a ruff, mypy and pytest gate in continuous integration.

Licensing is split by content type: the code under src/, scripts/ and tests/ is released under the MIT License, while the notebooks and prose documentation are released under CC BY 4.0.
